title: The Embodiment of Sex
paragraphs: After leaving the audience chamber, Father sat down in a chair in the room we were led to, looking exhausted.
“Phew… Well, at least it looks like we’ll be able to prove our innocence.”
“I think the conversation itself went smoothly.”
“That’s true. But, how should I put it… he’s quite the king in many ways.”
“I agree with you on that point, Shield Hero.”
The representative of the Shusaku race nodded. After all, this fellow is a native of this world. He must know quite a lot.
“It’s a rare experience to have the chance to see the ‘Lustful and Violent King’ in person, though…”
“That’s quite the nickname.”
“Well, he’s got all sorts of rumors and a colorful history, after all.”

I hear he had a peculiar hobby of abusing and embracing countless pigs? If we manage to capture Takt alive, he’d be the best person to handle those pigs. It’s precisely because we know Takt is dead this time that it’s so difficult to identify the pigs around him. In this regard, we have no choice but to rely on the Pig King’s ability to distinguish between his own pigs.
“There’s that famous quote from the King: ‘The more you torment them, the tighter they get,’ isn’t there?”

Father has taught me all sorts of things, from the characteristics of the Shusaku breed to the Pig King’s famous sayings. He’s quite an impressive pig in many ways. I have my reservations, but let’s keep him alive as long as he’s useful.
“I mean, is he really okay in every sense?”
“As long as we keep feeding him pork, he’s harmless.”
Hmm? Something about the unspoken parts of the previous loop feels a bit off. What is this memory?

A while after the wave ended, when I was staying in Faubrey, I feel like the Filolial I was raising went to visit the Pig King… and became friends with him. I can’t quite remember her face, but she was pestering King Faubrey while calling him “Piggy, Piggy.” Eventually, something happened that made me fly into a rage and storm in—and the scene I witnessed was… the Pig King clinging to me, crying as if begging for his life, looking utterly shocked… It must be some kind of mistake.

For me to not be able to remember Her Highness Filolial’s name or face… ugh… Is it that I’m mistaken, or that I’ve simply forgotten? For some reason, the image of the Pig King’s aides trying to get their work done while stifling their laughter is stuck in my mind. There’s no doubt my memory is vague.
But for now, I need to explain this to Father. Right… let’s talk about that.
“Apparently, his taste in men is like a mix of Ren and Itsuki, divided by two.”
“What kind of useless trivia is that…? I mean, does that king go for men too?”
“He’s the embodiment of sexuality, isn’t he?”
“I can’t really deny it. Well, it doesn’t seem like there’s any direct harm to us, so I guess it’s okay…?”

He seems a bit skeptical, but Father appears to have accepted it for now. Well, at the very least, he’s never been hostile toward us, so I think we’ll be fine. Even if he were to become hostile, I have no intention of losing to someone who’d only be able to handle Takt at best.
“They’ve promised substantial aid to the Heroes, haven’t they? It seems they’ll provide just about any kind of assistance.”
“That’d be a big help, but…”
Even considering that point, they’re not a bad partner to have. Oh? Panda is seizing the moment to draw money in the air with his hands.
“Lasa, I understand how you feel, but calm down.”
“What’s wrong with that? Having unlimited money to spend boosts motivation, and there’s no need to be shy about it. After all, there’s no limit to how much good gear you can get.”
“That’s the opinion of a mercenary on the payroll. It sounds just like one of those online game equipment discussions. I was sure you’d say something about using your power to live in luxury.”
“I think that’s fine, too. Shouldn’t we lay the groundwork while we still have the money?”
“Well, when it comes to armor, there are some excellent items that drop, but if you want something even better—whether it’s materials or anything else—money is absolutely essential.”

The most impressive armor I’ve ever seen was the one Father wore at the very end of the first world. That was the kind of item that could only be completed by combining the world’s finest materials and craftsmen. You could say it’s the pinnacle. Above all, some weapon enhancements require money, after all. You can never have enough money. I suppose these were the reasons why Father in the first world was so obsessed with money.
“As for weapons, the hero can probably handle them on their own, but once you’ve gathered a party, you can’t take that lightly.”
By the way, I really enjoy putting together equipment for Lady Filolial. Claws are the standard gear, but each of Lady Filolial’s companions has their own preferred weapon.
“I’m not sure about stretching the interpretation to include permission for luxury… but it seems like a complex issue.”
“Well, as for me, my body is my most valuable asset, so I want to eat well and build up my strength.”
“Yes, we’d be delighted if you’d work closely with the Hero.”
Just as the Shusaku representative agreed with Panda, Panda suddenly straightened up with a start.
“N-no, that’s not what I meant!”
“Ah… I feel like my expectations are being misinterpreted in a weird way. We’ve completely gone off track here.”
And so, we managed to secure a promise of aid from Faubrey as well. With this, wouldn’t you say the issue with Takt is more or less resolved?
“Well… there are still various other matters to tackle, like facing the waves, but given our connection to the place, should we go inspect Shieldfreeden, which we once occupied?”
“That country is also in the midst of chaos. I think we should wait and see a little longer…”
“You could argue that’s precisely why we should go, couldn’t you? We need to capture the representative who’s on the run, right? Even if he is wanted by the authorities.”
“That’s certainly true, but…”
That’s right. Those guys are pretty high-level, after all. Your average knight or adventurer wouldn’t stand a chance against them.

“The Hero has to take on the Waves, and we can’t just ignore the Waves in the Shieldfreeden region just because things are chaotic. If the Takt faction is wreaking havoc there, we need to set things right even more so.”
Just as I’d expect from Father. You’re saying that just because the enemy was in control doesn’t mean it’s okay for the people living there to suffer.
“What a hassle… Can’t we just show up when the waves hit?”
“Well… that’s true, but now that we’ve won, it’ll work to our advantage if we take care of a few things. According to what Motoyasu-kun found out, faith is apparently part of a Hero’s power.”
That’s right. Father used to say that trusting others and being trusted by them also strengthens us.
“Besides, it’d be a real pain if we got hindered by the citizens of Shieldfreeden right in the middle of a wave.”
“You guys are the Heroes, right? How could that even happen?”
“It can happen, you know?”

After all, the First World’s Father was once attacked by the Knights of Melromarc even though he was conducting rescue operations during the First Wave. So it’s not entirely implausible that the locals might try to hinder the Hero’s activities.
“It seems Motoyasu has a hunch about this.”
“Of course I do.”
“Huh… So there really are people out there who are completely fearless…”
“That’s just how it is. That tendency becomes even stronger, especially in enemy nations.”

“Attacking the Hero in the chaos of the waves is a barbaric act so heinous it wouldn’t be forgiven even if the penalty were death, but if it’s under the pretext of inspecting Shieldfreeden and dealing with the remnants of Takt, then I can accept it.”
The representative of the Shusaku race agreed as well. He seems a bit uneasy, but leave it to me.
“Siltvelt has no intention of withholding its cooperation with the Hero’s activities.”
“Yeah. Ultimately, we’d like to keep Shieldfreeden nicely in check.”
For these reasons, we decided to return to Siltvelt from Faubrey before heading to Shieldfreeden. But before that… well.
“Come to think of it, while it’s understandable that Itsuki is dead, is there a reason no one’s asked about Ren, the Sword Hero?”

“According to intelligence from Melromarc, it’s been confirmed that the Sword Hero, who didn’t participate in the battle, is currently active in the Zeltoble area, so I hear Faubrey avoided forcing him to report for duty.”
“Well, it is Ren, after all. I seem to recall he was quite dissatisfied with his treatment in Melromarc and said he was going to flee to Zeltoble.”
“Huh? Motoyasu, did you meet Ren?”
“That’s right… It was before this loop, but I believe I met him after the first wave from Melromarc that summoned us.”

It’s starting to come back to me now. After his comrades were beaten to death by someone impersonating Father, and then the people of Melromarc reprimanded him—using my strength as a benchmark—for not training hard enough, he finally reached his breaking point.
“He casually mentioned seeking asylum in Zeltoble, so I’m sure that’s correct.”
“Huh… Well, given Melromarc’s attitude, I guess it can’t be helped… With the Eclair incident as well, it looks like we’ll have to step in and quell the Melromarc wave ourselves.”

That Trash has already been ousted, after all. The Pope of the Three Heroes Church has also been dealt with. I suppose that means the Queen has already returned home. If that’s the case, we can probably expect public order to be restored to some extent. At the very least, there shouldn’t be any incidents where we’re attacked immediately after being summoned.
“I’ll show you I can quell the unrest right away.”
“Yeah, that’s right. We might end up having to ask Motoyasu-kun for help.”
“What about Naofumi and Sakura?”
“We’re here too, you know.”
“Kou too—”
“Everyone’s counting on you. Do your best.”
“Yeah—I’ll do my best!”
Father gently strokes Sakura-chan’s head. Oh… what a lovely sight.

But Sakura-chan is Filo-tan. I’ve been putting this completely on the back burner, but I really should start thinking about how to turn Sakura-chan into Filo-tan. It’s a problem I need to take quite seriously…
“That’s right! Since we’re here, how about we scout a Doctor in Faubrey!?”

The Doctor is a leading expert on monsters. The chances that he possesses enough wisdom to easily turn Sakura-chan into Filo-tan are… low, but it can’t hurt to ask. Besides, health checkups for the Filolials are important, after all. Well, Yuki-chan and the others seemed a little uncomfortable about it, but health is important.
“What’s with the sudden change of subject, Motoyasu-kun?”
“While the investigation into Shieldfreeden is important, since we’ve come all the way to Faubrey, I don’t think it’d hurt to reach out to a Doctor who could be useful in the future.”
“A Doctor, huh? Is he in Faubrey?”
“That’s right. Normally, he’d have been driven out by Takt and come to the estate of Father in Melromarc, but since we defeated Takt…”
“Huh… What kind of person is he, exactly?”
“He used to take care of Lady Filolial’s health. He’s also done research on Lady Filolial in the past.”

That reminds me of when the four heroes came to Faubrey. We had a heated debate with a Filolial producer back then. If we could get his help, it might not be impossible to turn Sakura-chan into a Filo-tan.
“Well, if he’s someone we can rely on, maybe we should ask him? After all, we have a lot of Filolials among us, and it’d be a real problem if any of them got sick.”
“Our monster doctors here in Siltvelt are quite skilled, though.”
“But you’re saying, Motoyasu-kun, that you know someone even better. It might be a good idea to at least have him come talk to us or something like that.”

The Doctor’s skills are undeniable. Moreover, he’s a man of such character that even Father from the first world acknowledges him. Well, he does seem to place a bit too much emphasis on safety, but that’s also a testament to his skill.
“Understood. If you say the Hero is needed for the battles ahead… I’ll submit a request to Faubrey. Since we have King Faubrey’s permission, it should be approved.”
“So, Motoyasu, shall we go see this Doctor?”
“Understood.”
This brings us one step closer to Filo-chan. So, before heading back to Siltvelt, we decided to go to Faubrey to settle things with the Doctor.
Relying on our memories, we head toward the district where Faubrey’s Doctor is located. Yuki-chan and the others are watching with keen interest.

It brings back memories. From what I can see… there doesn’t seem to be any damage. In the loop from the last time I visited Faubrey, the folks at the Homunculus Research Institute went on a rampage and caused an accident. So far, there doesn’t appear to be any damage.
“There are so many different monsters here, it almost feels like a zoo. They might actually be pretty skilled, though.”
“Huh… I remember traveling to all sorts of places, but this is a pretty unusual spot.”
“You’re a mercenary, after all. Do you go on all kinds of adventures too?”

“I’ve done a bit of treasure hunting… but most of it’s just commissions. Basically, stuff like gathering medicinal herbs growing in remote areas or escorting merchants. Fighting monsters to level up is important too, but if you’re an adventurer long enough, your level goes up on its own.”
“Huh…”
“Well, one of the real thrills is hunting down rare monsters or something like that, then selling their materials for money.”
And so, Panda is having a lively conversation with Father. Since Father is a great listener, Panda is really opening up.
“Don’t you have any interest in dressing up and working as a street vendor or something?”
